# Florian Herrengt

> Software engineer and consultant.

Updated: 2026-11-14.

Software engineer working in the field since 2010. I design and deliver
production systems end to end, led engineering teams of up to four, and
co-founded and sold my own software business. Strongest in full-stack product
engineering (TypeScript, Node, React/React Native, GraphQL) and data-intensive
backends (AWS serverless, real-time analytics, ML pipelines). A good fit for
teams that need a senior or lead engineer who owns outcomes — architecture,
delivery and product decisions — not just tickets. Based in Greater London,
UK.

## Key achievements

- **Built and sold Nocodelytics** — analytics for Webflow sites. Co-founder
  from June 2021, ran engineering, rebuilt the entire platform. Among the
  first apps on the Webflow Marketplace; featured in the Webflow Conf 2022
  keynote (https://youtu.be/aUXgKFEQugQ?t=3487). Grew past 1,000 tracked
  sites and 5,000+ installs, processing hundreds of millions of events at
  hundreds of requests per second — well within the architecture's limits.
  Acquired October 2024; I stayed through the handover until December.
- **Redesigned the Financial Times article page** — the page millions of
  daily readers see, including the breaking-news alert pages. Also built the
  data pipelines behind my FT's article recommendations and the GPU/EC2
  training pipelines for the data science team.
- **Led TRIM-IT's platform build** — project lead, four engineers, data
  platform delivered in six months: React Native iOS/Android apps, GraphQL
  API on serverless, infrastructure fully in CloudFormation. Covered by the
  BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news/stories-47711610), Evening Standard and
  Hacker News. The founders went on to raise their next round — their
  achievement, enabled in part by the product.

## Technical case studies

### Event analytics at scale on TimescaleDB (Nocodelytics)

Problem: ingest every interaction (clicks, links, forms, page views, Webflow
CMS items, plus third-party tools like Jetboost, Wized, Memberstack and
Outseta) from 1,000+ sites — millions of events per day, with sharp spikes
when a customer's site gets publicity — and serve dashboard queries fast
enough that several concurrent metrics feel instant.

Design: a tracking script with automatic event capture; a metric creator
that is simple on the frontend but compiles to advanced SQL on the backend;
storage in TimescaleDB (time-series on Postgres). The key decision was a
wide table layout instead of a normalized one:

- Measured result: queries up to **6x less costly** with the wide table
  layout.
- The write-up, with schema and benchmarks, was published by Timescale on
  their own engineering blog:
  https://www.tigerdata.com/blog/how-to-use-wide-table-model-to-reduce-query-cost-in-timescaledb

### Nocodelytics: end to end, from rebuild to exit (2021 - 2024)

I joined Sarwech Shar as co-founder in June 2021 — Nocodelytics was an MVP
with paying customers — and rebuilt the entire platform: a TypeScript
monorepo with Webflow OAuth sign-up, a React/GraphQL dashboard, a
lightweight tracker script, and an event pipeline designed for volume. Team
of three at the peak. From mid-2023 I ran the whole company alone through
to the sale: product, engineering, infrastructure, operations, support.

- Product: per-element clicks, forms, searches and CMS analytics —
  categories other analytics tools did not cover for Webflow. Very large
  CMS collections (sites with 10,000+ items) were hard to support and a
  selling point; CMS event attribution worked without any Webflow hooks,
  by parsing rendered pages to infer the collection and item behind a
  click.
- Pipeline, measured in production: Fastify ingestion, NATS JetStream as
  the durable queue, enrichment workers, batched inserts into ClickHouse
  (events moved from TimescaleDB in 2023). I built and benchmarked a Go
  rewrite of the ingestion API and a full AWS Kinesis/Glue/Athena
  serverless pipeline before choosing the self-hosted path on cost and
  operability.
- Operations: a single self-managed k3s cluster — Longhorn, Velero,
  Traefik, kustomize staging/production overlays, self-hosted Gitea,
  Drone CI and a private container registry. I was the platform team.
- Quality bar: 1,400+ commits over four years, all written by me, before
  AI assistants — every commit was hand-written work; 125 test files;
  end-to-end tests that verify events land in ClickHouse, run against
  live staging on every deploy; SQL migrations applied automatically in
  pipelines; a scheduled production data-integrity check ("events
  inserted in the last 2h") with email alerts; daily encrypted backups;
  DPA and GDPR self-service. No incident ever took the product down —
  for an analytics product, downtime means events missed forever.
- Traction: 1.6k installs in the first weeks of the Webflow Marketplace
  launch (November 2022), later the 5,000+ installs category; customers
  included Makerpad and Webflow agencies; testimonials from Jetboost's
  founder and NoCode.Tech; billing via Stripe and native Webflow
  Marketplace billing. When Webflow opened Designer extensions in 2023,
  I shipped ours in about two weeks — charts inside the Webflow designer.

### Recommendation engine for my FT (Financial Times)

Problem: recommend articles to paying readers, where "more reading = better"
is the wrong metric and good is hard to measure.

What I tried first: deep learning — LSTM (long short-term memory) networks
in Keras. Result after about three months: one or two points of improvement,
negligible, over simply recommending the top front-page articles. I dropped
it and count that as my mistake.

What shipped: a simpler rule-based system backed by data — keyword matching,
K-means clustering, and entity-follow expansion (a Brexit follower gets new
articles mentioning the Prime Minister). User testing showed readers were
satisfied.

A year after I left, the 2019 RecSys paper "Are We Really Making Much
Progress?" showed the same finding field-wide: simple baselines matching
neural recommenders. Lesson kept: always try the simple approach first.

| Jan 2025 – now | Independent | See below |

Role notes:

- **Skim.it**: first hire of an ML/NLP document-summarization startup (later
  Deeper Insights, a Forbes top-ten AI consulting firm). Microservices for
  resource-intensive deep-learning models, Node.js API, React front end, CI
  for the ML infrastructure. Early AWS Lambda and serverless user from 2015,
  learning at the AWS Pop-up Loft in London.
- **Lightful**: integrated the Twitter firehose through AWS Kinesis; built
  K-means clustering and audience-overlap analysis to recommend content and
  posting times; effectively the most senior engineer on the team.
- **Financial Times**: article-page redesign (see key achievements),
  accessibility work, data pipelines, my FT recommendations (see case
  study), knowledge-transfer training.
- **Wanderpay** (2018): two-week fixed-price build of the initial product
  for a travel-BNPL fintech — lender integrations plus the loan-application
  UI. The co-founder's recommendation above links this build to their seed
  round. Andy Davis (10x10) saw this work and recommended me for TRIM-IT.
- **TRIM-IT** (Sep 2018 – Mar 2019): see key achievements.
- **ContentCal**: social-platform integrations, introduced GraphQL to the
  team, CI with GitHub Actions and automated tests, on a legacy codebase
  integrated gradually rather than rewritten. ContentCal was later acquired
  by Adobe (announced December 2021) — a company outcome I contributed to as
  one of the engineers.
- **2025 – now**: after selling Nocodelytics I travelled and explored new
  business opportunities, and returned to independent software engineering
  and consulting alongside technical writing and conference speaking.

## Background (optional, deep context)

- Education: master's in computer science (Ingésup) as a French work-study
  apprenticeship (alternance) — one full week at a company, one week in
  class, for five years, 2010–2014. The employer and regional council paid
  the training costs. This is why my CV shows four years of employment
  before graduation.
- Childhood: computers since early childhood; RPG Maker games with scripts
  as a kid; at 17 spent a year building my high school's website in a small
  French town, self-taught HTML/CSS, including a map page for the open house
  days — the demo that got me my first job.
- Early roles in one line each: Intuitive Travel — iOS/geo-located sound app
  Terra Sonata, PHP/MySQL, mentored daily by the founder. Haubourdin Town
  Hall — jQuery/Ajax apps used by residents, network restructure. Agora
  Finance/BNP Paribas — regulation-heavy corporate work, centralized log
  management, first single-page application (Sensa, Ext JS); they offered to
  hire me on graduation.
- Side project with public impact: during COVID (2020) I organized a
  3D-printing operation making face shields for NHS workers — raised funding
  via GoFundMe, production at Craft Central, feedback loop with medical
  staff, 1,000+ shields by May 2020:
  https://blog.florianherrengt.com/3d-printing-ppe.html
- People worth knowing about: Kevin Rion (mentor, Adjust Your Set), Joshua
  (Skim.it CTO, close friend), Miroslav Batchkarov (Skim.it, now Google
  DeepMind), Sarwech Shar (Nocodelytics co-founder, now VEED), Sait Cham
  (Wanderpay), Andy Davis (10x10), Harry and Harris (ContentCal engineers).
